claim: A systematic review/meta-analysis of 83 studies (no RCTs) with mean/median follow-up >=5 years found median long-term seizure-free proportions of 66% after temporal lobe resection, 46% after occipital/parietal resection and 27% after frontal lobe resection.

bibliographic_record.authors: Téllez-Zenteno JF, Dhar R, Wiebe S
bibliographic_record.title: Long-term seizure outcomes following epilepsy surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis

supporting_passage: The median proportion of long-term seizure-free patients was 66% with temporal lobe resections, 46% with occipital and parietal resections, and 27% with frontal lobe resections.
passage_location: Abstract (unstructured), results sentences. Abstract only (full text not read). Europe PMC REST API (resultType=core, abstractText) for PMID 15758038; https://europepmc.org/abstract/MED/15758038; accessed 2026-11-01

population_and_design.design: systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies (articles since 1991, >=20 patients, any age, mean/median follow-up >=5 y)
population_and_design.n_studies: 76 articles yielding 83 studies (78 resective, 5 non-resective); 40 temporal, 25 grouped temporal+extratemporal, 7 frontal

endpoint.reported_endpoint: proportion long-term seizure free (median across studies); outcome classification system varied across studies
endpoint.protocol_mapping_v1: seizure free -> favourable; original classification heterogeneous across included studies

reported_observation: Median long-term seizure freedom 66% temporal, 46% occipital/parietal, 27% frontal; year of operation, follow-up duration and outcome classification most strongly associated with outcomes.
author_inference: Long-term (>=5 y) seizure-free rate after temporal resection was similar to short-term controlled studies; extratemporal and palliative surgery consistently lower.
contradictions: de Tisi 2011 (single-centre cohort, n=615 adults) reports lower survival-based seizure freedom (52% at 5 y, 47% at 10 y) using time-to-first-seizure Kaplan-Meier, a stricter definition than cross-sectional 'seizure free at last follow-up' used by many included studies.
overlap_note: Pooled observational cohorts; may include earlier reports from centres later published separately (e.g. NHNN London series behind de Tisi 2011) -- cohort overlap to_verify. Does not include Wiebe 2001 (no RCTs included).
